what_happened.line: Water commissioners voted to accept a new rates and fee schedule that includes a redeposit fee for returned checks the bank charges the district for.
Commissioners voted to authorize a contract with Stantec for design and bidding of the Mass Ave water main replacement.
The board moved to double sprinkler and fire protection connection fees, unchanged for decades, with a flat first tier for 0 to 20,000 square feet; the vote was not audible.
Red Dog was retained for snow retention rails on the garage and office roof, contingent on Rockwell not coming in lower.
Personnel policy and benefits changes were tabled, and the next meeting was canceled with an RFP for cellular on the tank pushed to Feb 9.

why_it_matters: Water district customers with sprinkler or fire protection connections face higher connection fees, and anyone whose check is redeposited faces a new fee.
The Mass Ave main design starts a project whose remaining funds the board described as insufficient, so a borrowing or annual meeting article is likely to come before voters.
watch_next: Feb 9 meeting, where the RFP for cellular on the water tank is expected.
Annual meeting article or borrowing for the Mass Ave water main, which the board said would be needed.

meetings.headline: Water commissioners will seek more quotes on garage snow-retention rails; the 2022 meeting schedule was approved.
meetings.summary: The Lunenburg Water District commissioners approved the October minutes and the 2022 meeting schedule, then discussed a quote for roof snow retention rails on the new garage and office and asked for more prices. The superintendent reported on a cell-equipment RFP, a tank painting estimate, a possible UV treatment building, new-building punch-list problems and possible stimulus money for the Hickory Hills well. A special meeting then elected a commissioner by ballot.

public_comment.topic: A resident asked the board to check roof pitch and ice-jam risk before installing snow retention clips.

votes.motion: Approve the 2022 schedule of board of commissioners meetings

budget_items.topic: Snow retention rails, garage and office
budget_items.what_was_said: Red Dog of Fitchburg gave prices for the office, the garage and both; doing both costs a little over a thousand dollars more than the garage alone.
Members thought the price was high for snap-on clips and wanted other contractors to quote.
Prevailing wage requirements were said to drive the price up.

budget_items.topic: Painting the Chase Road tank exterior
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent got an informal price for painting the outside, with prevailing wage raising it.

budget_items.topic: Stimulus funds for Hickory Hills treatment
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner asked whether federal stimulus money could fund treatment at the Hickory Hills well; the superintendent said it was likely.
The superintendent is working with a landowner on exchanging for water connection fees or buying a piece of land.

decisions.decision: Superintendent to get a couple more prices for the snow retention rails before deciding.
Aim to open proposals for the Chase Road tank cell equipment RFP at the December 15th meeting.
Board favored letting Sprint leave its equipment building and keeping the cable tray for a future carrier.
Superintendent to check with the attorney about discussing raises in executive session.

Commissioners approved the 2022 schedule of board meetings by voice vote.
The board aims to open proposals for the Chase Road tank cell equipment RFP at the December 15th meeting.
The board favored letting Sprint leave its equipment building and keeping the cable tray for a future carrier.
A special meeting elected a commissioner by ballot, and the superintendent will check with the attorney about discussing raises in executive session.

why_it_matters: The rail price, tank painting estimate and a possible land purchase or exchange for a UV treatment building are all costs the district may pass on to water customers.
Federal stimulus money for Hickory Hills well treatment was described as likely, which would bear on how much of that work ratepayers fund themselves.
watch_next: The December 15th meeting, when the board aims to open proposals for the Chase Road tank cell equipment RFP.
Further quotes for the snow retention rails, which the superintendent is to bring back before the board decides.
